summary: Mohican-Memorial State Forest tower built in 1934 at 80 feet; still standing, not staffed, stairs open to climbers at their own risk when weather allows.

access.note: stairs open when weather allows, at climbers' own risk; in Mohican-Memorial State Forest

events.note: built in 1934 and 80 feet tall; described in October 1934 as the nucleus of a new fire protection unit not yet organized
James Stevenson, the property caretaker, was to occupy the tower that season
farm fire south of Loudonville burned four acres of timber; spotted from the tower by Stevenson
Elmina Rohrbaugh employed at the tower from 1949
Elmina Rohrbaugh named as the observer in the tower in March 1967
National Historic Lookout Register registration date September 2, 2014

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says 125 feet. The marker, the ODNR-sourced newspaper story and the 2018 article say 80 feet. The record uses 80 feet (24.4 m).

notes_for_editor: The original ODNR page returned HTTP 404; the Ashland Source reprint of the ODNR story was used instead. The 1978 closure date is statewide, not a Mohican-specific date, and no source gives the year Mohican itself was last manned. The marker photo credit (Craig Doda, 2025) was not added because no license was shown. The register's 125-foot figure is the only outlier.
